summary: A DBA‑initiated autovacuum configuration change (cfg-2903) at 08:00 increased background work on the shared ledger‑db, pushing CPU to ~95 % and active connections to ~190. This resource exhaustion caused PostgreSQL to cancel statements, producing a flood of timeout errors (F1) that directly drove order‑service p99 latency from ~150 ms to >5 s (F2). No new deployments occurred, and request traffic remained steady, ruling out a code change or load surge. The root cause is the config_change on ledger‑db.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Autovacuum config change caused DB resource exhaustion → statement timeouts → order-service latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor reduction at 08:00 increased background vacuum activity, driving CPU and connection usage on ledger-db to near‑capacity, which caused statement timeouts that manifested as high order-service latency.

causal_chain.claim: config change → DB CPU & connections spike
Statement timeouts → order-service p99 latency spike

ranked_hypotheses.title: Sudden load surge on ledger-db saturated capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A spike in traffic to ledger-db (e.g., from other services) saturated CPU and connections, causing timeouts that impacted order-service.

causal_chain.claim: External traffic surge → DB CPU & connections spike

assumptions: Other services generated a hidden traffic surge not captured in order-service request_rate
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted by stable order-service request_rate and lack of evidence of other services' load

facts.statement: The incident manifested as order‑service latency >5 s and DB statement timeouts.

timeline.event: ledger‑db CPU and connections begin rising (F5,F6)
First statement timeout logged (F1) and order‑service latency spikes (F2)

recommended_actions.action: Rollback autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor to previous value (0.2) or tune to avoid high CPU load.
recommended_actions.rationale: Reverses the config change that triggered resource exhaustion (supports H1).

recommended_actions.action: Monitor ledger‑db CPU, connections, and autovacuum activity; add alerts for >80 % CPU or >150 active connections.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of similar resource‑exhaustion events.

recommended_actions.action: Review shared‑service usage of ledger‑db; consider isolating high‑traffic services or increasing DB capacity.
recommended_actions.rationale: Mitigates impact of any future config or load changes on a shared critical datastore.

data_gaps: No metrics from ledger‑db disk I/O or lock contention; could clarify if autovacuum caused I/O bottleneck.
No logs/metrics from other services that also use ledger‑db; would confirm whether the load surge was isolated to order‑service.

findings.statement: ledger-db statement timeout errors began at 2026-05-05T09:00:42Z in order-service logs

refs.quote: ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)

findings.statement: order-service p99 latency spiked from ~150 ms to >5 s starting at 09:00
No deployments of order-service occurred between 2026-05-04 and 2026-05-05
DB autovacuum configuration changed at 08:00 (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor from 0.2 to 0.1)
ledger-db CPU usage jumped to ~95 % at 09:00 and stayed high
ledger-db active connections rose from ~60 to ~190 at 09:00
order-service request rate remained stable (~230 req/s) through the incident
